newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Gdansk refinery raises fuel prices.
newsitem.headline: Poland's Gdansk refinery raises fuel prices.

text.p: Poland's second largest refinery, Gdansk, will raise its prices for leaded and unleaded petrol as well as diesel fuel by between five and 8.5 percent as of February 14, it said in a statement on Thursday.

The rise follows the finance ministry's decision announced earlier on Thursday to free all fuel prices and remove administrative limits on distributors' margins. The Gdansk refinery's spokeswoman Ewa Sielicka told Reuters the price of 94-octane leaded fuel would rise to 1.59 zlotys per litre from 1.51 zlotys and the 98 octane leaded to 1.72 zlotys from 1.62 zlotys per litre.
The price of the unleaded 95 octane petrol would go up to 1.55 zlotys from 1.46 zlotys and diesel fuel to 1.40 zlotys from 1.29 zlotys.
"The new prices are still competitive against imported fuel prices," the statement quoted Gdansk's head of marketing Krzysztof Naruszewicz as saying.
"At the same time they will allow the processing of crude oil in the refinery to become profitable again," he said.
As a result of the administrative controls, Polish refineries suffered reduced profits because they could not offset rising world crude prices by increasing domestic market prices.
The net profit of the Gdansk refinery last year fell by about 35 percent from 125 million zlotys in 1995 and one of its officials said last week it had suffered extra losses in the last three months.

"The rises will not compensate for the losses which we have suffered over the last months, and will not provide sufficient funds for the necessary modernisation of the refinery," Gdansk's financial head Stanislaw Pokojski said. -- Jan Strupczewski +48 22 653 9700
